84302ac4c6.q: How does working your way up from dishwasher to director of operations shape leadership approach and credibility with restaurant staff?
84302ac4c6.a: Having worked every position in a restaurant, from dishwasher to management, gives perspective to work with people with empathy. Understanding what team members experience daily, what tasks are challenging, and being able to give perspective on operational opportunities because you have done it before sets the tone for leadership and gives you clout among employees. When people know you made it to your level starting from entry-level work, it shows them a path forward and demonstrates that they do not have to stay in a starting position forever.
84302ac4c6.rq: My success is a byproduct of their success. So if I can help them be successful, and that goes with caring about them, understanding what they're going through personally, professionally, and trying to clear some of those hurdles for them.

8c3c7a1127.q: How should restaurant leaders balance empathy and challenging employees with maintaining operational performance and service goals?
8c3c7a1127.a: Leadership must start with perspective of the team member as a whole—you have to love people, care about them, and look out for their best interest. When giving feedback and encouragement toward the goal, position yourself as 'I'm here to help, I want you to be successful.' People give grace when they know your motive is to help, not to exploit. Success as a leader is a byproduct of employee success, so clearing hurdles and providing information for improvement, whether professional or personal, is essential. You must be honest but brutally honest when employees feel you are there to serve them, not judge them.

a60facf5b1.q: What role does modeling behavior play in restaurant leadership and setting operational expectations with staff?
a60facf5b1.a: Modeling behavior is critical because if you say something is important but never act on it, it is not actually important. When Table 100 gets busy, leadership gets involved in setting tables and handling tasks rather than only greeting guests. If you say a table should be ready one minute after guests leave but never demonstrate that yourself, staff understand it is only important for you to say it, not for the outcome to matter. Leaders must show through their actions that they are willing to pick things up, move things around, and get involved, which signals to the team that help will come when needed.

7377e83e02.q: How does Table 100 keep restaurant employees motivated without relying on external incentives?
7377e83e02.a: Motivation is not about getting people excited—they already arrive motivated when they take a job. The focus is on not demotivating them by avoiding poor leadership, harsh criticism, and placing them with low performers. Table 100 gives staff the task at hand and gets them to buy into the common goal of making guests happy. They provide a great team to work with, celebrate successes with simple recognition ('I saw what you did there, that was awesome'), and hold daily and afternoon pre-shift meetings at the same time every day to discuss operational improvements and how to be better than competitors.
7377e83e02.rq: My success is a byproduct of their success. So if I can help them be successful, and that goes with caring about them, understanding what they're going through personally, professionally, and trying to clear some of those hurdles for them.
